answer: Unrepeatable challenge provenance. Each identity must solve a freshly generated challenge whose seed derives from the prior block's ripple of transaction ordering, and the solution must embed a karst-like unique trace of that specific sequence. Since the seed changes every block, precomputation is useless; each identity costs one full sequential computation per registration, so N identities cost N times the sequential work. Duplicates fail because the trace won't match at dawn of the next validation round.
